title: さらに — furthermore / even more
summary: An adverb with two uses. It adds a further thing to what was said (“furthermore, on top of that”), and it shows a degree rising even higher (“even more”). It is somewhat formal and common in writing and speeches.

patterns.gloss: adds another point (さらに雨も降ってきた)
even more (さらに上手になりたい)

body.p: It piles on content of the same direction to what has been said, as in 風が強くなり、さらに雨も降ってきた and 値段が安い上に、さらに送料も無料だ. It goes well with particles such as も and まで. It is more formal than そして and それに and suits writing.

As in さらに上手になりたい, it means going one more step beyond the present state. A word of changing degree follows, such as 上手になる or 大きくなる. It is close to もっと but more formal, suggesting something added on top of what is already considerable.

examples.ja: 風（かぜ）が強（つよ）くなり、さらに雨（あめ）も降（ふ）ってきた。
examples.romaji: Kaze ga tsuyoku nari, sara ni ame mo futte kita.
examples.tr: The wind got stronger, and furthermore it began to rain.

examples.ja: 値段（ねだん）が安（やす）い上（うえ）に、さらに送料（そうりょう）も無料（むりょう）だ。
examples.romaji: Nedan ga yasui ue ni, sara ni sōryō mo muryō da.
examples.tr: Not only is the price low, but on top of that shipping is free.

examples.ja: 練習（れんしゅう）を重（かさ）ねて、さらに上手（じょうず）になりたい。
examples.romaji: Renshū o kasanete, sara ni jōzu ni naritai.
examples.tr: By practicing more and more, I want to get even better.

pitfalls: What you add goes in the same direction as before. For the opposite use しかし.
It is stiffer than conversational もっと. In casual talk use もっと or それに.
